title: The Last Alibi Revisited
premise: Ivo Okafor, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him both invaluable and isolated, is summoned when a drowned man is found wearing clothes stolen from Ivo's own closet — clothes that match a death he investigated thirty years ago in Lagos. As he re-examines the old case, Ivo discovers his perfect memory has been quietly edited: someone he loved, his late wife Adaeze, was the alibi for the original suspect, and her testimony may have been coerced. Racing against a killer who is eliminating everyone who remembers, Ivo must choose between preserving Adaeze's legacy and exposing the truth. In the end, he sacrifices his career and nearly his life to force a confession, finding that justice outside the law — and love beyond duty — is the only verdict that frees him.
about_author: Coral Sandoval is a former claims adjuster turned novelist who spent a decade reading other people's disasters on paper before writing her own. She lives in Lisbon with a dog named Verdict and an unhealthy interest in cold cases.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man Wore My Coat
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A body pulled from the harbor wears Ivo's own missing jacket and a watch engraved with a date from 1994. The police treat him as a suspect; his memory insists the items were stolen weeks ago. Emotional beat: uncanny dread — the past has literally dressed itself in his skin.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Perfect Recall
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with flashback to 1994 Lagos. He reconstructs the original drowning case he investigated as a young adjuster, where witness Adaeze provided the alibi that closed it. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling as he notices gaps in what he 'remembers.'

chapters.title: The Widow Who Lied Beautifully
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews the dead man's widow, Ngozi, who recognizes him and flinches at Adaeze's name. She hints the 1994 alibi was bought. Second body is found — another witness from the old file. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: What Memory Forgets on Purpose
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He interrogates his own recollections and finds seams: a night he cannot picture, a sentence Adaeze repeated like a script. His therapist suggests trauma editing. Emotional beat: vertigo — the one thing he trusted about himself is compromised.

chapters.title: The Man Who Paid for Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with retired detective Emeka Balogun, who worked the 1994 case and took payments from shipping magnate Chief Danjuma. Emeka knows someone is killing witnesses and drafts a confession letter. Emotional beat: guilt finally demanding interest.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Ivo finds a cassette Adaeze hid before her death: her voice describing how Danjuma threatened her family unless she gave the alibi. Ivo realizes she chose him partly to keep him close to the truth. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Every Exit Is Watched
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Danjuma's fixers tail him; his apartment is ransacked; the cassette vanishes but he has memorized it — his gift becomes the only unstealable evidence. Emeka is attacked. Emotional beat: hunted, cornered, resolute.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter
chapters.summary: Emeka's POV. He mails his confession to Ivo and to a journalist, then confronts Danjuma directly. The chapter ends mid-confrontation with a gunshot off-page. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the worst possible price.

chapters.title: Alibi for a Ghost
chapters.summary: Climax. Ivo lures Danjuma by threatening to 'misremember' evidence in his favor, then springs a recorded trap at the harbor where both drownings occurred. Danjuma confesses; the fixer turns on him. Ivo takes a knife wound protecting the recording. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into justice.

chapters.title: A Memory Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ivo's POV. Months later: Danjuma convicted, Emeka posthumously honored, the 1994 case reopened and Adaeze's name cleared. Ivo resigns from insurance work, keeping only the jacket returned from evidence. Final beat: peace — some memories are worth their weight in wounds.
